The late-diagnosed group is also the OLDER cohort (mean current age 34.6 vs 23.7 years), so the secular trend in population height runs AGAINST the finding and strengthens it. Against that: n=12, retrospective, single centre, and diagnosis age is confounded with everything else that changed in care between the two eras.

THE ANIMAL COUNTERPART OF THE HUMAN FINDING, and it localises the effect: radiographs showed generalised osteopenia and ACCELERATED EPIPHYSEAL OSSIFICATION with metaphyseal and suprametaphyseal lucencies that the authors call similar to human homocystinurics, and they describe the model as reproducing "accelerated skeletal growth, epiphyseal growth plate lesions". Tibiae were stronger, but strength was proportional to the increased length and cortical thickness, so there is no intrinsic material change - the bone is bigger, not better. High-dose dietary exposure producing a disease, in a fast-growing bird; not a model of therapeutic intent.

The authors note that Marfan and homocystinuria share long bone overgrowth, scoliosis and ectopia lentis from fundamentally different origins, which is the clue that the shared axis is the fibrillin microfibril and its control of TGF-beta rather than anything about collagen. IN VITRO ONLY: recombinant protein and dermal fibroblasts, no growth plate, no animal.

parameter: direction in which the fixed shape exponent biases the reported height change
conditions: prefactor P(n) = (pi/4) x Gamma(1+1/n) x Gamma(1+2/n) / Gamma(1+3/n) in v = P(n) x X(0deg) x E{X^2(90deg)}; computed by this atlas at 0.524 (n=2, spheroid), 0.626 (n=2.9, the value used), 0.785 (n=infinity, cylinder). Height = v / (P x E{X^2}), so P and the estimated height move oppositely.
uncertainty: DERIVED BY THIS ATLAS. n=2.9 was fixed once, on one animal at one age, and held for all three ages. A cell that becomes taller relative to its width is by construction moving toward the cylinder end of the family, i.e. toward higher n and higher P, so holding n fixed OVERSTATES the height rise. The estimator's fixed-shape assumption errs in the same direction as the claim it is used to support. Magnitude unknown, because nobody measured n at either age.

parameter: growth-rate budget reconstructed from hunziker1989's own tables

But it shows that "cells produced per column per day is unchanged" is not an independent measurement: proliferative cells per column is itself PZ height divided by the model-estimated PROLIFERATIVE cell height (226/8.1=27.9 vs 27 printed; 171/9.6=17.8 vs 18; 78/8.2=9.5 vs 9). So the height estimator sits in both the numerator and the denominator of the budget, and enters only as the RATIO h_term/h_prolif, in which any common multiplicative bias cancels exactly. That ratio rises just 4.1% (3.85 to 4.01) between 21 and 35 days, against the +23% headline. Under this factorisation the +19.6% growth rise is 0.638 x 1.500 x 1.234 - a 36% fall in proliferative cells per column, a 50% rise in cycles per day, and the height term. Same arithmetic, different attribution; "almost exclusively cell height" holds only if turnover is treated as measured rather than derived.

parameter: internal consistency of hunziker1989 Table 2 under its own estimator

unit: implied E{X^2(90deg)} divided by the square of the reported mean diameter
conditions: back-solving E{X^2(90deg)} = 5v / (pi x X(0deg)) from the printed terminal height, diameter and volume at each age, and comparing with the square of the printed diameter. E{X^2} must be greater than or equal to the square of the mean for any distribution.
uncertainty: DERIVED BY THIS ATLAS, unreplicated. At 21 and 35 days the triples are feasible and imply a diameter CV of 0.374 and 0.312. At 80 days they are NOT: the required E{X^2} is 21% below the square of the printed mean, which no distribution permits. The reported 80 d diameter would have to overstate the true width by at least 12%. That is precisely the bias the method paper attributes to this estimator in hypertrophic cells, so the most likely reading is a known, variable, zone-dependent width bias rather than an arithmetic error. The alternative readings - that E{X^2(90deg)} came from the unfolding algorithm rather than from the printed diameter row, or that a different exponent was used at 80 days - cannot be separated from the published tables. Either way the printed height and diameter columns are not mutually consistent under one fixed shape model.

Abolition by a CARTILAGE-SPECIFIC receptor knockout localises the effect to chondrocyte NPR-B and excludes the rest.

The drug protects a peptide the tissue must already be making; where CNP and NEP expression are low it has nothing to act on. Whether the human equivalent window is infancy, mid-childhood or the pubertal growth spurt is UNKNOWN, and getting it wrong would produce a null that looks like a refuted mechanism. Mouse 3-4 weeks is peri-pubertal and roughly the peak growth period, but mouse and human growth plate timelines are not superimposable - the human plate closes, the mouse plate does not.
